items.title: Bounded-runs hook: stop denying 'command -v' tool probes; clean up test tempdirs
items.spec: scripts/bounded_runs.py: in strip_prefix (the transparent-wrapper loop that treats `command` as TRANSPARENT, ~:37 and ~:231-237), when the word is `command` and the next word is `-v` or `-V`, return no command (None/empty) so `command -v luacheck`, `command -V lizard`, `command -v luacheck lua` and `command -v luacheck lizard` produce check()==[] and the hook stays silent. Plain `command luacheck .` must still be denied (command stays a transparent wrapper otherwise). Update the module docstring wrapper sentence to note the -v/-V exception. scripts/test_bounded_runs.py: add pass cases ('command -v lizard', 'command -V luacheck', 'command -v luacheck lua') to test_mentions_are_not_runs (or a new test_command_v_probe_is_not_a_run), and a deny case 'command luacheck .' to test_plain_runs_are_refused; add a HookScript case asserting the hook JSON for 'command -v luacheck lizard' is empty (no permissionDecision). Replace every bare tempfile.mkdtemp() (repo() helper ~:17, XDG_CACHE_HOME ~:136, HOME ~:155 and ~:184) with a shared helper that creates the dir and registers self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, d, True). CLAUDE.md Build/test bullet for test_bounded_runs.py (':91', '20 cases') and any DEPENDENCIES.md case count: update to the count the runner actually reports. No plugin.json version bump (CLAUDE.md:107 asks for one only when a command/agent is added or removed).

Add the tempdir cleanup helper and convert all mkdtemp call sites. 3. Implement the -v/-V exit in strip_prefix; rerun until green. 4. Update the case count in CLAUDE.md (and DEPENDENCIES.md if it states one) and the docstring. 5. Commit 'DC-01: Stop the bounded-runs hook denying command -v probes'.

items.title: ka0s-bounded: kill the whole tree on timeout when non-interactive; recompute slots while waiting
items.spec: scripts/ka0s-bounded: (a) timeout (~:98-100): build cmd=(timeout -k 10 "$secs" ...) and add --foreground only when [ -t 0 ] (interactive terminal, keeps Ctrl-C working); non-interactive runs (Claude's Bash tool) then let timeout signal the whole process group so forked children (and the slot-pool lock fd they inherit from :78) die with the run. Rewrite the CLOCK header comment (:18-19) to say --foreground is used only on a terminal and why. (b) slot pool (~:66-93): when KA0S_KIT_SLOTS is unset/invalid, recompute slots from MemAvailable inside the outer wait loop on every pass (same formula max(1, floor(avail*0.6/slot_mb))), so a run started under memory pressure can take slot.2+ once memory frees; the 'waiting for a slot' message still prints once (it may report the slot count at first wait). Factor MemAvailable reading into a small function used both at startup and in the loop. scripts/test_bounded_runs.py BinWrapper: add test_timeout_kills_children: run bin/ka0s-bounded bash -c 'sleep 47 & sleep 47; echo done' (use a unique sleep length to grep for, e.g. 'sleep 4711') with KA0S_KIT_TIMEOUT_S=2, KA0S_KIT_CGROUP=off, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL and a cleaned-up XDG_CACHE_HOME; assert rc==124 and, after a short poll, `pgrep -f 'sleep 4711'` finds nothing (kill any survivor in cleanup so a red run leaves no process). DEPENDENCIES.md:47 coreutils row: reword the 'timeout --foreground -k 10' evidence to the conditional form. README Hooks section: if it describes --foreground or the slot count as fixed at start, align it. CLAUDE.md test_bounded_runs case count updated to the runner's figure.
items.steps: 1. Write test_timeout_kills_children; run it and confirm it fails (survivor present). 2. Make --foreground conditional on [ -t 0 ]; rerun green. 3. Refactor MemAvailable read and move the slot recompute into the wait loop (guarded by KA0S_KIT_SLOTS unset); hand-check with KA0S_KIT_SLOTS unset and set (exact count honoured). 4. Update header comment, DEPENDENCIES.md:47, README, CLAUDE.md count. 5. Commit 'DC-03: Kill the whole run on ka0s-bounded timeout and recompute slots while waiting'.

items.spec: New scripts/test_normalize_eol.py: stdlib unittest, LF endings, '#!/usr/bin/env python3' shebang, git mode 100755 (git add --chmod=+x). Each case builds a tempdir git repo (TemporaryDirectory/addCleanup) with a .gitattributes, writes a file, pipes the hook JSON {"tool_input":{"file_path":<path>}} into bash scripts/normalize-eol.sh, and asserts bytes. Cases: CRLF arm (`* text=auto eol=crlf`): LF file -> CRLF, mixed file -> all CRLF; LF arm (`* text=auto eol=lf`): CRLF file -> LF; already-correct file stays byte-identical (both arms); no eol declared -> untouched; `*.png binary` (or -text) file in a CRLF repo containing \n bytes -> untouched; file outside any repo -> untouched; empty/missing file_path -> exit 0, nothing written; symlinked file (alias.lua -> target.lua in a CRLF repo) -> target converted AND alias still a symlink — this case is decorated @unittest.expectedFailure with a comment naming DC-05, so the suite stays green until the fix lands. items.title: Delete the stale origin/main branch (owner go-ahead only)
items.spec: Remote-only housekeeping, no commit: origin/main points at d2ed30d (initial commit, ancestor of master); default branch is master. Gated: only after the owner explicitly approves, run git push origin --delete main in ../dev-copilot. Until then (and if declined) record the item in exceptions.tsv as 'awaiting owner go-ahead' / 'declined'. Proof when done: git ls-remote --heads origin main prints nothing. Never touch master or any other ref.
items.steps: 1. Confirm git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main master. 2. Ask the owner at the final go-ahead (bundle it with the merge approval). 3. On yes: git push origin --delete main; add an exceptions.tsv row with the proof command. On no: exceptions.tsv row 'declined by owner'.
items.verify: git ls-remote --heads origin main (empty after deletion); exceptions.tsv row DC-14 present with that command
